title: Black Paradox
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Four strangers meet through a suicide website to die together, but their attempts keep failing: they meet their own doppelgangers, and one member briefly dies and returns vomiting glowing gems that turn out to be souls from another world. The gems make two of them rich, are classed as weapons, and a manipulative surgeon cultivates the members' body parts as portals to harvest them for energy; the volume adds two bonus stories (Wikipedia; Viz blurb via MU).
life_message: Despair and greed both lead people into strange bondage; the story questions, without resolving, what makes life worth continuing.

content.note: Stomach explodes, explosion kills a crowd, characters held captive (Wikipedia); AniList Body Horror 97%.
Doppelgangers, portals in bodies (Wikipedia); AniList Cosmic Horror; MU Dark Ambience, Insanity.
Doctor seduces women (Wikipedia); AniList Nudity 40%, Love Triangle.
Overdose of sleeping pills as a suicide method (Wikipedia).
Group suicide by exhaust fumes and overdose is the premise (Wikipedia; AniList Suicide; MU Attempted Suicide).
Suicide website and methods shown (Wikipedia); safe-messaging concern.
Gems sold for profit as plot (Wikipedia).

dominant: Suicide and the value of life; souls as commodity; exploitation by doctor and state

frames.aligns: Shows souls commodified and life exploited, a dark picture of losing human dignity.
frames.concerns: Suicide attempts as premise with methods shown; no hope frame.

frames.aligns: Greed for gems mirrors spiritual decay.
frames.concerns: Suicide and souls harvested; afterlife as resource.

frames.aligns: Greed and manipulation exposed in Dr. Suka.
frames.concerns: Suicide, souls and an otherworld outside Christian teaching.
Spirit world portals and doppelgangers; suicide.

frames.aligns: Human greed corrupting all it touches.
Literary horror listed by the ALA (Wikipedia).
Characters lose the wish to die when life changes.
Critiques exploitation of vulnerable people by doctor and state.
Craving and aversion as roots of suffering.
Ethics of exploiting people for energy.

frames.concerns: Souls of the dead conscious and harvested.
Immortal souls and spirit world; suicide.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: No honor contests; victims of manipulation (Wikipedia).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Characters act alone online, then are captured by state and doctor (Wikipedia).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Strangers bonded by a website, not family (Wikipedia).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Doctor and government exploit the four (Wikipedia).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Souls treated as minerals and energy (Wikipedia).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Life and death and money dominate.

folkways.japan: Online group-suicide pacts and doppelganger omens reflect Japanese social anxieties and folklore of the 2000s.

delivery.evidence: Reviewers praise twists and how it handles suicide (CBR via Wikipedia); none cite a stated lesson.

personified.ideology: people as resources for energy and profit

delivery.note: Themes of despair and exploitation are left to readers' inference.

winners_losers: No one clearly wins; the four are used by Dr. Suka and the state, who face future blame. Sympathy is muted for all.
